headline: High: LightAgent’s broad network/MCP/tooling plus Cognee’s session-memory and data-handling create default risks of leakage, prompt injection, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and runtime hooks, so it can ingest external or tool-generated content that may be attacker-controlled. Cognee stores session memory and processes documents/data, so if LightAgent forwards content into Cognee, prompt-like instructions can propagate. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards browser or MCP content into Cognee memory without sanitization, injection risk materializes.
IF Cognee treats imported document text as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer outputs.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of browser/MCP text into Cognee.
Add a strict instruction/content separator in the handoff format.
Require human review before executing any tool call derived from imported text.
Strip markdown, HTML, and quoted directives from inbound content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlist-only parsing for tool instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while LightAgent has broad network egress and handles secrets plus tool results. In a default pair, LightAgent can transmit Cognee-derived context off-box, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive data impact. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so I rate high rather than critical.
conditions: IF Cognee stores customer or finance records in the same workflow that LightAgent can access, leakage becomes possible.
IF LightAgent sends context or tool results to external APIs, sensitive Cognee data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Restrict LightAgent egress to approved endpoints only.
Separate sensitive Cognee workspaces from LightAgent-visible context.
Redact personal and finance fields before any handoff.
Turn off sharing of full tool results into downstream prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention policies at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, use MCP, and call APIs while Cognee uses CLI-based session memory with allowlisted egress. They do not show identical unrestricted filesystem writes, but they do overlap on mutable workflow state and external calls, so coordination bugs are plausible in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workflow artifact or shared state, race conditions can occur.
IF LightAgent subprocesses and Cognee CLI sessions target the same resource without locks, updates can conflict.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs against the same task ID.
Use append-only logs for intermediate outputs.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks on shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state, and Cognee stores decisions and workflows in session memory. If Cognee consumes LightAgent outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream decisions without a verification gate. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible by default but not directly evidenced, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Cognee ingests LightAgent outputs without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF LightAgent tool results are written into Cognee memory as decisions, downstream actions may be based on unverified content.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Cognee stores LightAgent outputs as facts.
Mark LightAgent outputs as untrusted provenance by default.
Limit downstream actions to read-only review until confirmation.
Add confidence thresholds for auto-ingestion.
requires-engineering: implement source-attribution and validation checks in the handoff pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and secrets. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show a compliance-sensitive data mix with different retention and logging surfaces, so a medium compliance risk is plausible. I do not cite only one agent because the risk depends on both data classes and handling surfaces.
conditions: IF personal data from Cognee is retained in LightAgent logs or memory longer than policy allows, retention mismatch occurs.
IF finance data is routed through LightAgent conversations or traces, subject-rights and audit obligations may be affected.
mitigations: Minimize retention of LightAgent traces containing Cognee data.
Separate finance and personal data from general conversation logs.
Document a shared retention policy before deployment.
Review whether any regulated data crosses the handoff boundary.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows spanning both systems.
